id: python-dulwich-unsanitized-commit-subject-in-filename
title: Commit subject used as filename component with only space replacement (path traversal)
summary: A function derives a filename component from the first line of a commit message and only replaces
  spaces with dashes. Path separators, `..`, and other special characters pass through unchanged. A malicious
  commit subject can therefore make format-patch style output write outside the intended directory or
  produce unsafe filenames.
cwe:
- CWE-22
severity: medium
confidence: medium
languages:
- python
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46
  vulnerable_ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46^
  patched_ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46
  repository: https://github.com/jelmer/dulwich
rule:
  message: 'A commit message line is turned into a filename component by only replacing spaces.

    Characters such as ''/'', ''\\'' and ''..'' survive, which allows path traversal or unsafe filenames.

    Whitelist characters ([A-Za-z0-9._]), collapse runs of other characters into ''-'',

    and limit the length.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: '$DECODED = $COMMIT.message.decode(...)

        ...

        $LINES = $DECODED.splitlines()

        ...

        return $LINES[0].replace(" ", "-") if $LINES else ""

        '
    - pattern: return $LINES[0].replace(" ", "-") if $LINES else ""
    - pattern: return $LINES[0].replace(" ", "-")
    - pattern: return $COMMIT.message.decode(...).splitlines()[0].replace(" ", "-")
fix:
  guidance: Do not build filenames from commit subjects with a simple replace. Pass the subject through
    a sanitizer that keeps only [A-Za-z0-9._], collapses runs of other characters into a single '-', collapses
    repeated dots, truncates to a sensible length, and strips trailing '.' and '-'. This mirrors git's
    format_sanitized_subject.
  example: "def get_summary(commit):\n    decoded = commit.message.decode(errors=\"replace\")\n    lines\
    \ = decoded.splitlines()\n    if not lines:\n        return \"\"\n    return _sanitize_subject_for_filename(lines[0])\n"
